evidence: Cic. Att. 8.9.3: circum vīllulās nostrās (Lewis & Short)
Ov. M. 13.821: multae quoque vallibus errant
terms.comment: Going about with no fixed way or goal. It also, and very often, means to be wrong (see wrong); errāns is someone who has lost his way (quī errantī cōmiter mōnstrat viam, Enn. ap. Cic. Off. 1.51).

evidence: Cic. Div. 2.80: volucrēs hūc illūc passim vagantēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Moving freely here and there, of people, flocks, birds, bees; the word for roaming at will rather than being lost.

evidence: Liv. 5.44: vagī per agrōs pālantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a crowd or a herd that has scattered; mostly in the participle, pālantēs. Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: vagātur omnis turba sordidae chortis, argūtus ānser gemmeīque pāvōnēs
phrases.english: the whole grubby farmyard crowd wanders about, the honking goose and the jewelled peacocks

phrases.latin: hoc pecus omne meum est, multae quoque vallibus errant
phrases.english: all this flock is mine, and many more are wandering in the valleys

phrases.latin: apēs, ut ajunt, dēbēmus imitārī, quae vagantur et flōrēs ad mel faciendum idōneōs carpunt
phrases.english: we should copy the bees, as they say, which wander about and pick the flowers fit for making honey
